quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is a lot of traffic.

questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because motorcyclists and other drivers can collide there more easily.

questions.question: When checking tire pressure:

options.text: Looking at the tire is a good way to check it.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare your tire height to another tire.

questions.explanation: Always use a tire gauge to check pressure before riding. A tire that is not fully inflated may still look fine, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: When you are going to turn, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should always use a turn signal.
Only need a turn signal if there are pedestrians nearby.
Only need a turn signal at a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should always use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when you turn or change lanes. Use it even if you think everyone can see what you are doing. Other vehicles may be nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Signs that show rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. Riders must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake light.
Less noticeable than a car's brake light.
Less important than a car's brake light.
Easier to see than a car's brake light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake light.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle brake light is usually not as noticeable as a car's brake light. Flash your brake light before you slow down or stop so other drivers see you.

questions.question: The best thing you can do to survive a crash is:

options.text: Ask other riders for safety tips.

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most important thing you can do to reduce injury or death in a crash.

questions.question: Goggles will:

options.text: Work as well as a face shield.
Give the same protection as a windshield.

questions.explanation: Goggles protect only your eyes. A face shield protects your entire face and is better than goggles. A windshield does not protect your face like goggles or a face shield do.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes gently, slow down, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oily spots, shadows, dirt, gravel, and bridges because they have less grip than dry pavement.

questions.question: Gloves can:

options.text: Make it hard to control your motorcycle and should not be worn.
Give you a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves give you a better grip on your handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Which surface does NOT have poor traction?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all have poor traction. Dry pavement is safer for motorcycles than these surfaces.

questions.question: Who is most likely to have a motorcycle crash?

options.text: Those who have completed a safety course.

questions.explanation: Beginning riders who are untrained and unfamiliar with their motorcycle are most likely to crash.

questions.question: What should you do for motorcycle safety?

options.text: Assume everything on your motorcycle will work properly.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: Small mechanical problems on a motorcycle can be very dangerous. Check your motorcycle carefully before every ride.

questions.question: What material offers the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather clothing provides the best protection for motorcycle riders. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs completely when riding.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle, similar to using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: If you drink just one alcoholic drink, what happens?

options.text: Your judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
There is usually no effect on the body.
There is an effect on the body, but it only lasts a short time.
There is an effect on the body, but drinking coffee will eliminate it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect the skills you need for safe riding. Your body must have time to eliminate the alcohol. Drinking coffee does not help.

questions.question: What is a simple way to make your motorcycle more visible?

options.text: Attach a large flag to the motorcycle frame.
Ride on the shoulder whenever possible.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Use your turn signals and brake light correctly. Wear bright, reflective clothing to be more visible.

questions.question: What helps reduce the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?

options.text: Not allowing a passenger on the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most important thing you can do to prevent head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcycle rider should be ready for:

options.text: A car suddenly pulling out of a parking space into traffic.
Other drivers seeing the motorcycle and staying out of its way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car suddenly pulling out of a parking space into traffic.
questions.explanation: A parked car may suddenly pull into traffic. Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars on your right to stay as far away as possible from this danger.

questions.question: When approaching a bump or pothole, rise slightly off your seat so:

options.text: You can jump off if needed.
Your legs can absorb the shock.
Other drivers can see you better.
You can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off the seat allows your legs and joints to absorb some of the impact. This prevents the bump from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: What does the SEE strategy stand for?
questions.explanation: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy for safe riding. SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Regular glasses or sunglasses are not enough. In Vermont, you don't have to wear eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still recommended.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator slow down?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders can slow down by downshifting. Know that downshifting does not turn on your brake lights.

questions.question: Which of the following should you NOT check on your tires?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires for air pressure, tread, and general wear.

questions.question: What should you do about checking your mirrors?

options.text: Check them as part of your regular scanning routine.
Avoid them because they distract you.
Avoid them because other drivers can see you.
Check them only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them as part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: You need to know what is behind you for safety. Check your mirrors often as part of your regular scanning routine.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.
